```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(shiny)
library(shinyWidgets) # knobs
library(SpatialEpi)   # pennLC data
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)

data(pennLC)
ref <- pennLC$data |>
  group_by(race, gender, age) |>
  summarise(r = sum(cases) / sum(population), .groups = "drop")   # state rates
d <- pennLC$data |>
  left_join(ref, by = c("race", "gender", "age")) |>
  group_by(county) |>
  summarise(O = sum(cases), E = sum(population * r), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(county = as.character(county), SIR = O / E)
pa <- st_as_sf(pennLC$spatial.polygon) |>
  st_set_crs(4326) |>
  st_transform(5070) |>
  mutate(county = names(pennLC$spatial.polygon))
d <- d[match(pa$county, d$county), ]               # same order as the map

O <- d$O                                           # observed cases
E <- d$E                                           # expected cases
tc <- function(x) sub("Mck", "McK", tools::toTitleCase(x))
w_of <- function(name, k) E[d$county == name] / (E[d$county == name] + k)   # trust
pct  <- function(x) paste0(round(100 * x), "%")

by_size  <- order(d$E)                             # county menu, small to large
counties <- setNames(d$county[by_size],
                     paste0(tc(d$county[by_size]), " (E = ", round(d$E[by_size]), ")"))
rr <- seq(0.4, 2, by = 0.005)                      # relative risk axis

risk_class <- function(x) cut(x, c(0, 0.67, 0.83, 0.95, 1.05, 1.2, 1.5, Inf),
                              c("< 0.67", "0.67-0.83", "0.83-0.95", "0.95-1.05",
                                "1.05-1.2", "1.2-1.5", "> 1.5"))
risk_fill  <- scale_fill_brewer(palette = "RdBu", direction = -1, drop = FALSE,
                                name = "Relative risk")
exc_cols   <- c("Probably lower (< 0.2)"  = "#2c7bb6",
                "Uncertain (0.2-0.8)"     = "grey90",
                "Probably higher (> 0.8)" = "#d7191c")
exc_class  <- function(p) cut(p, c(0, 0.2, 0.8, 1), labels = names(exc_cols),
                              include.lowest = TRUE)

map_panels <- function(values, panels, i, classes = risk_class, fill = risk_fill) {
  m <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(values), function(j)
         mutate(pa, value = values[[j]], panel = panels[j])))
  m$panel <- factor(m$panel, panels)
  ggplot(m) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = classes(value)), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
    geom_sf(data = pa[i, ], fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.9) +   # chosen county
    facet_wrap(~ panel, ncol = 2) +
    fill +
    theme_void(base_size = 13)
}

clicked_county <- function(cl) {                   # county under a mouse click
  if (is.null(cl)) return(NULL)
  hit <- st_intersects(st_sfc(st_point(c(cl$x, cl$y)), crs = st_crs(pa)), pa)[[1]]
  if (length(hit) == 0) NULL else pa$county[hit[1]]
}

knob <- function(id, label, value, min, max, colour) {
  knobInput(id, label, value = value, min = min, max = max, step = 1,
            angleOffset = -125, angleArc = 250, thickness = 0.3, lineCap = "round",
            fgColor = colour, inputColor = colour, width = "140px", height = "140px")
}

play_knob <- function(button, id, values, interval) {   # a Play button turns a knob
  on <- reactiveVal(FALSE)
  observeEvent(input[[button]], {
    on(!on())
    if (on() && input[[id]] >= max(values)) updateKnobInput(session, id, value = values[1])
    updateActionButton(session, button, label = if (on()) "❚❚ Pause" else "▶ Play")
  })
  observe({
    req(on())
    invalidateLater(interval)
    isolate({
      nxt <- values[values > input[[id]]][1]
      if (is.na(nxt)) {
        on(FALSE)
        updateActionButton(session, button, label = "▶ Play")
      } else updateKnobInput(session, id, value = nxt)
    })
  })
}
```

Small counties have unreliable SIRs, so we pull them toward the state average,
1. The question is **how hard to pull**. A single number, $k$, decides that.

## Part 1. What $k$ does

<div class="step">
Each county's best guess is a weighted average of **its own SIR** and **the
state average, 1**:

$$
\text{best guess} \;=\; w \times \text{SIR} \;+\; (1 - w) \times 1,
\qquad w = \frac{E}{E + k}
$$

- $E$ is the county's expected cases: **how much data it has**.
- $w$ is **how much we trust the county's own SIR**, from 0% to 100%.
- $k$ is counted in expected cases too. **A county with $E = k$ is trusted
  exactly halfway** ($w$ = 50%). Counties bigger than $k$ are trusted more,
  smaller ones less.

| | Potter ($E$ = `r round(E[d$county == "potter"])`) | Philadelphia ($E$ = `r format(round(E[d$county == "philadelphia"]), big.mark = ",")`) |
|---|---|---|
| $k$ = 5 | trusted `r pct(w_of("potter", 5))` | trusted `r pct(w_of("philadelphia", 5))` |
| $k$ = 50 | trusted `r pct(w_of("potter", 50))` | trusted `r pct(w_of("philadelphia", 50))` |
| $k$ = 500 | trusted `r pct(w_of("potter", 500))` | trusted `r pct(w_of("philadelphia", 500))` |

**Small $k$:** almost every county keeps its own SIR. **Large $k$:** only big
counties keep theirs; small counties are pulled to 1.
</div>

**What you see below.**

- **Left:** every county is a dot. Across: how much data it has ($E$). Up: how
  much we trust its own SIR ($w$). The dashed line is at $E = k$.
- **Middle:** the chosen county's **posterior curve**: which relative risks are
  plausible. Green area: the **95% interval**. Red dotted: its SIR. Black
  dashed: the state, 1.
- **Right:** its numbers.
- **Maps:** raw SIR, best guess, and the low end and high end of the 95%
  interval. Click a county to choose it.

**Predict first.** Turn $k$ up. What happens to the best-guess map? To Potter?
To Philadelphia?

```{r part1}
fluidRow(
  column(4, selectInput("county1", "County", counties, selected = "potter"),
            helpText("Or click a county on a map.")),
  column(4, knob("k", "k", 20, 1, 500, "#2c7bb6")),
  column(4, br(), br(), actionButton("play_k", "▶ Play"),
            helpText("Turns k from 1 to 500."))
)
fluidRow(
  column(4, plotOutput("trust", height = "290px")),
  column(5, plotOutput("curve", height = "290px")),
  column(3, br(), tableOutput("numbers"))
)
plotOutput("maps1", height = "470px", click = "click1")

play_knob("play_k", "k", c(1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 50, 70, 100,
                           150, 200, 300, 400, 500), 900)
observeEvent(input$click1, {
  cty <- clicked_county(input$click1)
  if (!is.null(cty)) updateSelectInput(session, "county1", selected = cty)
})
i1 <- reactive(match(input$county1, d$county))

output$trust <- renderPlot({
  k <- input$k; i <- i1()
  pts <- data.frame(E = E, w = E / (E + k))
  ggplot(pts, aes(E, w)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = k, linetype = 2) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, colour = "grey70") +
    geom_point(colour = "#2c7bb6", size = 2.2, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_point(data = pts[i, ], size = 4.5, shape = 21, fill = "orange") +
    annotate("text", x = k, y = 0.04, label = paste("E =", k), hjust = -0.1) +
    scale_x_log10(limits = c(4, 1500)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(100 * x, "%"), limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(title = "Trust, every county",
         x = "Expected cases E (log scale)", y = "Trust in own SIR, w") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 13)
})

output$curve <- renderPlot({
  i <- i1(); a <- input$k + O[i]; b <- input$k + E[i]
  ci  <- qgamma(c(0.025, 0.975), a, b)
  cur <- data.frame(rr = rr, dens = dgamma(rr, a, b))
  ggplot(cur, aes(rr, dens)) +
    geom_area(data = subset(cur, rr >= ci[1] & rr <= ci[2]), fill = "darkgreen", alpha = 0.25) +
    geom_line(colour = "darkgreen", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = d$SIR[i], colour = "red", linetype = 3, linewidth = 1) +
    labs(title = paste0(tc(d$county[i]), ", k = ", input$k),
         x = "Relative risk", y = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 13)
})

output$numbers <- renderTable({
  i <- i1(); k <- input$k; a <- k + O[i]; b <- k + E[i]
  data.frame(
    ` ` = c("Expected cases, E", "SIR", "Trust, w", "Best guess",
            "Low end (95%)", "High end (95%)"),
    Value = c(sprintf("%.0f", E[i]), sprintf("%.2f", d$SIR[i]),
              pct(E[i] / (E[i] + k)), sprintf("%.2f", a / b),
              sprintf("%.2f", qgamma(0.025, a, b)), sprintf("%.2f", qgamma(0.975, a, b))),
    check.names = FALSE)
})

output$maps1 <- renderPlot({
  a <- input$k + O; b <- input$k + E
  map_panels(list(d$SIR, a / b, qgamma(0.025, a, b), qgamma(0.975, a, b)),
             c("Raw SIR (no pulling)", "Best guess",
               "Low end of the 95% interval", "High end of the 95% interval"),
             i1())
})
```

<div class="step">
**What you should see.**

- **Small $k$:** all dots are near the top (every county trusted), and the
  best-guess map looks like the raw SIR map.
- **Large $k$:** small counties drop to the bottom (not trusted), and the
  best-guess map fades to white: they are pulled to 1. The low-end and
  high-end maps also move closer together.
- Philadelphia stays near the top for any $k$: it has so much data that we
  always trust it.
</div>

## Part 2. INLA does not know $k$, so it tries several values

Which $k$ is right? Nobody knows. But we can **test** any value of $k$
against the data.

### How do we know how plausible a value of $k$ is?

<div class="step">
Remember the **funnel plot**: even if every county had the state's risk, SIRs
would spread out **by chance**, more in small counties. About 95% of them would
fall within

$$1 \pm 1.96 \sqrt{1/E}.$$

$k$ adds **real** differences between counties on top of chance. If $k$ were
the right value, about 95% of SIRs would fall within a wider band:

$$1 \pm 1.96 \sqrt{1/E + 1/k}.$$

Small $k$ makes the band wide; large $k$ makes it close to the chance funnel.
So to test a value of $k$, **draw its band and see whether the 67 real SIRs
fit it**: about 95% inside, and filling the band rather than huddled in its
middle.
</div>

```{r bands, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 3.8}
band_k <- c(5, 100, 3000)
Eg     <- exp(seq(log(4), log(1500), length.out = 200))
bands  <- do.call(rbind, lapply(band_k, function(k)
  data.frame(k = k, E = Eg, lo = 1 - 1.96 * sqrt(1 / Eg + 1 / k),
             hi = 1 + 1.96 * sqrt(1 / Eg + 1 / k))))
dots   <- do.call(rbind, lapply(band_k, function(k) {
  h <- 1.96 * sqrt(1 / E + 1 / k)
  data.frame(k = k, E = E, SIR = d$SIR, outside = d$SIR < 1 - h | d$SIR > 1 + h)
}))
lab <- function(k) {
  n_out <- sum(dots$outside[dots$k == k])
  paste0("k = ", format(k, big.mark = ","), ": ", n_out, " of 67 outside")
}
bands$panel <- factor(sapply(bands$k, lab), sapply(band_k, lab))
dots$panel  <- factor(sapply(dots$k, lab), sapply(band_k, lab))

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = bands, aes(E, ymin = pmax(lo, 0), ymax = hi), fill = "purple", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(data = dots, aes(E, SIR, colour = outside), size = 1.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "black", `TRUE` = "red"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 2.2)) +
  labs(x = "Expected cases E (log scale)", y = "SIR") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 13)
```

<div class="step">
- **$k$ = 5:** the band is far too wide. Every county is inside, with lots of
  empty room: counties do not differ that much. **Not plausible.**
- **$k$ = 100:** the band fits. About 95% of counties are inside, and they fill
  it. **Plausible.**
- **$k$ = 3,000:** the band is almost the chance funnel, too narrow: too many
  counties (red) outside. Counties differ more than chance alone. **Not
  plausible.**

The purple **hill** below does this test for every $k$ from 1 to 700, more
precisely than by eye. For each $k$, R computes the probability of getting
exactly the 67 counts we observed, if that $k$ were true (one line,
`dnbinom()`). The higher that probability, the taller the hill.
</div>

<div class="step">
INLA's trick, in three moves:

1. **Try** several values of $k$ (here, spread evenly from 10 to 600).
2. **Weigh** each value by how plausible it is.
3. **Average** each county's curves, using these weights.

**How many values do we need?** We compare with the "full answer", which uses
3,000 values.
</div>

**What you see below.**

- **Left:** the purple hill: how plausible each $k$ is, from the band test
  above. The sticks are the values we try; a taller stick gets more weight.
- **Right:** the chosen county's averaged curve (thick green), built from the
  weighted curves (thin green). Dashed: the full answer.
- **Maps:** the probability that each county's risk is above the state's,
  $P(\text{RR} > 1)$, with our values and with the full answer.

**Predict first.** How many values will you need before the green curve sits on
the dashed one? Write down a number, then press **▶ Play**.

```{r part2}
fluidRow(
  column(4, knob("n", "Values of k tried", 2, 2, 35, "#1b7837"),
            actionButton("play_n", "▶ Play")),
  column(4, selectInput("county2", "County", counties, selected = "potter"),
            helpText("Or click a county on a map.")),
  column(4, br(), tableOutput("numbers2"))
)
fluidRow(
  column(6, plotOutput("weights", height = "300px")),
  column(6, plotOutput("average", height = "300px"))
)
textOutput("changed")
plotOutput("maps2", height = "330px", click = "click2")

play_knob("play_n", "n", c(2:10, 12, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35), 1200)
observeEvent(input$click2, {
  cty <- clicked_county(input$click2)
  if (!is.null(cty)) updateSelectInput(session, "county2", selected = cty)
})
i2 <- reactive(match(input$county2, d$county))

plausibility <- function(k) {                      # log scale: higher = more plausible
  sapply(k, function(kk) sum(dnbinom(O, size = kk, mu = E, log = TRUE)))
}
try_values <- function(n_values, k_min = 10, k_max = 600) {
  k <- seq(k_min, k_max, length.out = n_values)    # 1. try
  h <- plausibility(k)
  data.frame(k = k, weight = exp(h - max(h)) / sum(exp(h - max(h))))   # 2. weigh
}
full <- try_values(3000, 1, 3000)                  # the full answer

hill <- data.frame(k = 1:700)
hill$height <- exp(plausibility(hill$k) - max(plausibility(hill$k)))

p_above <- function(t) sapply(seq_along(O), function(i)        # 3. average
  sum(t$weight * pgamma(1, t$k + O[i], t$k + E[i], lower.tail = FALSE)))
p_full  <- p_above(full)

tried <- reactive(try_values(input$n))

output$weights <- renderPlot({
  t <- tried()
  ggplot(t, aes(k, weight)) +
    geom_area(data = hill, aes(k, height * max(t$weight)), fill = "purple", alpha = 0.15) +
    geom_segment(aes(xend = k, yend = 0), colour = "#1b7837", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_point(colour = "#1b7837", size = 3) +
    labs(title = paste(input$n, "values of k and their weights"),
         x = "k", y = "Weight") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 13)
})

output$average <- renderPlot({
  t <- tried(); i <- i2()
  parts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(t)), function(j)
    data.frame(j = j, rr = rr, dens = t$weight[j] * dgamma(rr, t$k[j] + O[i], t$k[j] + E[i]))))
  avg <- aggregate(dens ~ rr, parts, sum)
  ref <- data.frame(rr = rr, dens = sapply(rr, function(x)
           sum(full$weight * dgamma(x, full$k + O[i], full$k + E[i]))))
  ggplot(avg, aes(rr, dens)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 2) +
    geom_line(data = parts, aes(group = j), colour = "darkgreen", alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_line(data = ref, colour = "grey40", linetype = 2, linewidth = 1) +
    geom_line(colour = "darkgreen", linewidth = 1.4) +
    labs(title = "Averaged curve (green) vs full answer (dashed)",
         x = paste("Relative risk,", tc(d$county[i])), y = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 13)
})

summary_one <- function(t, i) {                    # one county, averaged curve
  a <- t$k + O[i]; b <- t$k + E[i]; w <- t$weight
  q <- function(p) uniroot(function(x) sum(w * pgamma(x, a, b)) - p, c(0.1, 5))$root
  c(sum(w * a / b), q(0.025), q(0.975), sum(w * pgamma(1, a, b, lower.tail = FALSE)))
}

output$numbers2 <- renderTable({
  i <- i2()
  out <- rbind(summary_one(tried(), i), summary_one(full, i))
  data.frame(` ` = c(paste(input$n, "values"), "Full answer"),
             `Best guess` = out[, 1], `Low end` = out[, 2], `High end` = out[, 3],
             `P(RR > 1)` = out[, 4], check.names = FALSE)
}, digits = 2)

p_now <- reactive(p_above(tried()))

output$changed <- renderText({
  paste0(sum(exc_class(p_now()) != exc_class(p_full)),
         " of 67 counties have a different colour than in the full answer.")
})

output$maps2 <- renderPlot({
  map_panels(list(p_now(), p_full),
             c(paste("P(RR > 1) with", input$n, "values"), "P(RR > 1), full answer"),
             i2(), classes = exc_class,
             fill = scale_fill_manual(values = exc_cols, drop = FALSE, name = NULL)) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
})
```

<div class="step">
**What you should see.**

- **2 to 4 values:** one value of $k$ takes almost all the weight, and it is
  not the top of the hill. The curve is too narrow, and on the map, counties
  that should be red or blue are grey.
- **About 8 values:** the green curve sits on the dashed one, and the maps
  agree.
- **25 or 35 values:** nothing changes any more. We could keep adding values
  forever, but it would only cost time.
</div>

## And BYM2?

BYM2 works the same way, with two unknown settings instead of one: $\sigma$,
how much counties differ (it plays the role of $k$), and $\phi$, how much a
county borrows from its neighbours rather than from the state. INLA tries
values of both on a grid, weighs them, and averages. In R-INLA, one option sets
how many values it tries:

```{r inla, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
control.inla = list(int.strategy = "grid", dz = 0.75)   # default; smaller dz = more values
```
